summary: Bounded revision of the Linux iDMA P4M validator plus its host-model tests. (1) idma_p4m_finish() gains a stricter frozen-record envelope: sequence != 0, observer_status exactly 4 (not merely bit 40 clear), window cycle counter non-zero and equal to legacy counter 0, and flags restricted to bits 0..2. (2) Batch identifier validation is added: issue/done/startID/endID/first/last must each be <= IDMA_EXPERIMENT_MAX_TRANSFERS, first/last must be contiguous (last = first + done - 1) when work completed, the opening stock's first retired ID must equal startID, and a closing stock must continue past the last retired ID (endID = last + 1); with no retirement a carried opening entry must close unchanged (closing stock 1, endID = startID). (3) Opening-edge-issue must imply a single opening entry, and carry-done is tied to strict carry: carrydone == (strictcarryflag && done > 0). Solo keeps all words 2..12 zero. (4) The unarmed helper no longer returns success: idma_p4m_finish() returns run_error (or -EIO when none) if the observer was never armed. (5) idma_gap_program_readback() additionally refuses a sticky backend batch error read back immediately before launch. (6) The host harness good P4M fixture is made ID-coherent (endID 0x101 for first/last 0x100) and new good/bad rows are added (zero-A-progress boundary variants, strict carry, opening edge issue, unknown flag, zero cycles, raw status, ID sequence, ID overflow, sticky error, direct unarmed finish); tests/test_idma_scheduler.py gains the matching case names. No run_session duplication, no other subsystem touched, no test executed here.

edits.old:
static bool p4m_bad_counts, p4m_bad_status, p4m_bad_readback, p4m_cap_missing;
static u64 p4m_window[16];

checks: Build the host model: cc -std=gnu11 -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I<build> <build>/scheduler.c -o <build>/scheduler (as tests/test_idma_scheduler.py setUpClass does); expect a clean -Werror build with the new u64 locals and bools.
Run tests/test_idma_scheduler.py and require exit 0 for every CASES entry plus CACHE_CASES; each must print 'PASS <case>'.
p4m_ok must still succeed with the corrected fixture window[9]=0x101 (endID == last retired ID + 1 for first=last=0x100, done=1).

New success rows must return 0 with allocations==frees: p4m_zero_a_progress_drained (closing stock 0, endID 0), p4m_zero_a_progress_pending (closing stock 1, endID = last+1), p4m_strict_carry_ok (opening stock 1, edge issue 0, flag bit2 set, carrydone 1), p4m_open_edge_ok (opening stock 1, edge issue 1, flag bit2 clear, carrydone 0).

New bad rows must return -EIO with allocations==frees and must otherwise satisfy window[4]+window[2]==window[3]+window[5]: p4m_bad_unknown_flag (flag bit3), p4m_bad_zero_cycles (window[1]=0), p4m_bad_id_sequence (last != first+done-1), p4m_bad_id_overflow (endID = 2^32+1 while first=last=2^32).
p4m_bad_status must still return -EIO (observer_status 4|BIT(40) rejected by the exact-4 check and by observation_finish).
p4m_sticky_error must return -EIO (idma_gap_program_readback sees BATCH_CONTROL bit32 set after the gap readback), with allocations==frees and no pending device, and p.experiment.status==-EIO.
p4m_direct_finish_not_armed must assert idma_p4m_finish(unarmed, run_error=0)==-EIO and idma_p4m_finish(unarmed, run_error=-ETIMEDOUT)==-ETIMEDOUT.

Regression: p4m_solo_ok, p4m_bad_conservation, p4m_bad_ids, p4m_bad_bank, p4m_bad_flags, p4m_bad_carry, p4m_readback_mismatch, p4m_timeout, p4m_interrupt, p4m_old_hw, p4m_cap_missing and all non-p4m cases must keep their existing return codes.
Kernel build of the driver is explicitly deferred; do not claim it from these host-model results.
risks: Field mapping assumption: window[2]=issue, window[3]=done, window[4]=opening stock, window[5]=closing stock, window[6]=carry-done, window[7]=opening-edge issue, window[8]=startID, window[9]=endID, window[10]=first retired ID, window[11]=last retired ID, window[15]=flags (bit0=has_a, bit1=valid, bit2=strict carry). This was inferred from the existing validator and the harness fixture; if the P4M bank map differs, the new index references must be corrected before the kernel build.

The contiguous-batch rule 'endID == last + 1' is applied only when a closing stock exists (window[5] != 0). That conditioning is what allows the p4m_zero_a_progress_drained boundary variant to succeed; an unconditional reading of the instruction would reject any window with done>0 and closing stock 0.

'Zero A progress' could not be derived from the harness because p4m_window[] is a static fixture, not a function of run activity. It is realised as the two closing-stock boundary variants (drained vs one pending) with the aggressor still configured; confirm this matches the intended P4M semantics.

idma_gap_program_readback() now performs one extra read of IDMA_BATCH_CONTROL_OFFSET immediately before launch; on real hardware this must be a side-effect-free status read. It is inserted only after the gap readback, so batch_configure/batch_collect are unaffected.

p4m_bad_carry still fails two ways (window[6] > window[4] and the new carry-done equality) because the opening stock is 0 in that row; it was left unchanged to keep the change bounded. An isolated carry-done bad row (opening stock 1, strict-carry bit set, carry-done 0) was intentionally not added.
idma_observation_finish() still returns 0 when unarmed without a run error; only idma_p4m_finish() was hardened, so a future caller of the observation helper directly could still see a false success.
No test or compiler was executed for this proposal; all PASS/exit-status statements above are acceptance criteria for Codex to verify, not observed results.
